bib.title: Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Jia, Yang, Xia, Chen, Parekh, Pham, Le, Sung, Li, Duerig (Google Research), "Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision" (ALIGN), ICML 2021 (PMLR 139). arXiv:2102.05918v2.
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/08-multimodal-engineering/sources/jia-2021-scaling-up-visual-vision-language.pdf

COVERAGE: All 14 pages and all 61,259 chars read, including Appendix A (near-duplicate removal) and Appendix B (SimLex-999). I only skimmed the references.

CLAIMS (most important first)
1. The dataset is 1.8B English alt-text pairs. It went through only light frequency-based filtering, not the full Conceptual Captions cleaning pipeline. Text filters: drop alt-texts shared by more than 10 images, alt-texts with rare tokens, and alt-texts under 3 or over 20 unigrams. Image filters: drop porn, keep shorter side >200px and aspect ratio <3, drop near-duplicates of test images.
   quote: "we trade quality for scale by relaxing most of the cleaning steps... a much larger (1.8B image-text pairs) but noisier dataset" (p3)
2. The model is a dual encoder: EfficientNet-L2 (global pooling) for images and BERT-Large ([CLS] plus a linear projection) for text, both trained from scratch. The loss is symmetric normalized-softmax contrastive with in-batch negatives gathered across all cores. Batch 16,384 on 1,024 TPUv3 cores, 289px images, about 12 epochs, label smoothing 0.1, learnable temperature initialized at 1.0.
   quote: "We train the model on 1024 Cloud TPUv3 cores with 16 positive pairs on each core. Therefore the total effective batch size is 16384." (p4)
3. Retrieval vs CLIP (Table 1, Flickr30K 1K test, MSCOCO 5K test). Zero-shot R@1, ALIGN vs CLIP: Flickr image→text 88.6 vs 88.0; text→image 75.7 vs 68.7; COCO image→text 58.6 vs 58.4; text→image 45.6 vs 37.8. So the gain sits in text→image; image→text is about even. Fine-tuned ALIGN: Flickr 95.3 / 84.9 and COCO 77.0 / 59.9, ahead of cross-attention models such as UNITER and Oscar.
   quote: "CLIP 88.0 98.7 99.4 68.7 90.6 95.2 58.4 81.5 88.1 37.8 62.4 72.2 / ALIGN 88.6 98.7 99.7 75.7 93.8 96.8 58.6 83.0 89.7 45.6 69.8 78.6" (p5)
4. Zero-shot ImageNet top-1 is 76.4 vs CLIP's 76.2, using CLIP's prompt ensembling, which itself adds 2.9 points. ImageNet-R 92.2 vs 88.9, ImageNet-A 75.8 vs 77.2, ImageNet-V2 70.1 for both.
   quote: "CLIP 76.2 88.9 77.2 70.1 / ALIGN 76.4 92.2 75.8 70.1" (p5)
5. Size vs noise ablation (EfficientNet-B7 + BERT-base, zero-shot MSCOCO, Table 10). At equal size, noisy data loses to clean data: ALIGN-3M gets image→text R@1 8.1 vs 18.9 for clean CC-3M. ALIGN-12M (4x the size) beats CC-3M at 23.8. Also from Table 9: full ALIGN data gives 55.4 vs 18.9 for CC-3M, and the small B3+BERT-mini model nearly saturates at 10% of the data.
   quote: "Despite being noisy, ALIGN data outperforms Conceptual Captions with only 4x size." (p7)
6. Embedding dim, negatives and temperature (EfficientNet-B5 + BERT-base, Table 8). Larger embedding dims help: 640→80 drops COCO image→text R@1 from 51.7 to 42.0. L2 uses 1376. Keeping only 50% or 25% of in-batch negatives hurts. The learned temperature converges to about 1/64. Fixed 1/64 and 1/128 are slightly better (52.2), while 1/32 collapses to 39.6.
   quote: "the baseline model that learns the temperature parameter (converged to about 1/64), some hand-selected, fixed temperatures could be slightly better" (p7)

Smaller points: frozen-feature ImageNet 85.5 and fine-tuned 88.64 (p6). Image+text embedding arithmetic works with a 2:1 text:image scale (p8). A multilingual version covers 100+ languages on 1.8B pairs (p9).

LIMITS
- The authors concede intra-modal retrieval is weaker. Text→text and image→image gains on CxC are small, and STS/SIS score below VSE++/DEI2T. They put this down to the cross-modal-only objective (p5).
- No released model or data. There is no audit of what is in the data, only a Social Impacts section noting harmful text, stereotypes and surveillance misuse, and saying analysis and balancing are "required" before production use (p9).
- The comparison with CLIP mixes changes: different architecture and different data curation, so the data effect is not isolated. Zero-shot image→text is roughly a tie with CLIP.
- No compute or latency cost comparisons beyond "44% FLOPS" vs NoisyStudent at test time. No study of what the remaining noise does once you are past 12M samples. The size-vs-noise ablation uses one model pair.
- Dated: it predates LAION and SigLIP. The "SOTA" claims are 2021-era.

BUILDS ON: Conceptual Captions pipeline (Sharma et al., 2018); visual-semantic embeddings (Frome et al., 2013; Faghri et al., 2018); normalized softmax loss (Zhai & Wu, 2019); contrastive SimCLR (Chen et al., 2020b); CLIP (Radford et al., 2021) as the closest prior work; EfficientNet and BERT (Devlin et al., 2019); LAMB optimizer (You et al., 2020).

CODE: none in the paper. The loss is Eq. 1–2 on p3: L_i2t = -1/N Σ log exp(x_i·y_i/σ)/Σ_j exp(x_i·y_j/σ), plus the symmetric t2i term.

FIGURES
- Figure 1, p2: "A summary of our method, ALIGN... Without any fine-tuning, ALIGN powers zero-shot visual classification and cross-modal search including image-to-text search, text-to-image search and even search with joint image+text queries." It shows the dual-encoder setup and the three query types in one view, which suits the multimodal-RAG paragraph.
- Alternative, Figure 5, p8: image±text query arithmetic ("+ beige", "- cars").
- Table 10, p8, is the clearest single display of size beating noise, but it is a table, not a figure.

PROBLEMS: Text extraction was clean. Figure text came out as stray labels, which I ignored. The Table 1 rows are flattened but readable. No embedded instructions. Typos in the source tables ("ImangeNet") are reproduced in the quotes as printed. Page numbers come from PDF page index (1-based).
